critical_steps: All eight original partitions reduce to four positive definite frame operators.
Their minimum eigenvalue is (7-sqrt(41))/2 and maximum eigenvalue is 4+sqrt(13).
The canonical duals are computed from exact inverse frame operators.
The partition taking indices 1 and 2 from the first canonical dual and index 3 from the second is contained in span{e1}.
If all constituent frame operators coincide, applying the common inverse to every weaving preserves uniform frame inequalities.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact enumeration of the four distinct two-dimensional weaving frame operators and exact computation of both canonical dual frames.
integrity.unproved_limits: No necessary-and-sufficient condition is claimed for arbitrary distinct constituent frame operators.

scientific_limitations: The finding refutes Corollary 2.5 as verified in arXiv:1709.05154v1 and v3; the subscription journal preview did not expose the theorem text, so no assertion is made that the version of record retained it verbatim.
A common frame operator is proved to be a sufficient repair, not a necessary characterization.
Later literature contains conditional canonical-dual weaving theorems and a distinct counterexample for canonical Parseval frames; these do not contain the checked source-specific counterexample.
title: Canonical duals of woven \(g\)-frames need not be woven
